title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel calls, result injection, and retries
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: the existing function/tool calling path supports single synchronous tool invocations but lacks ergonomic primitives for multi-tool orchestration, parallel invocations, injecting tool results back into the model loop, and robust retry semantics. This PR introduces a set of runtime and API changes to make multi-tool and parallel tool executions first-class: 1) API additions: a new 'tools' field in the OpenAI-compat function_call envelope that accepts an ordered list of tool descriptors and an optional 'parallel_groups' array to express which tools may be invoked concurrently. Each tool descriptor can declare idempotency metadata and a preferred retry policy string. 2) Runtime orchestration: a light-weight executor that schedules tool calls according to parallel_groups and dependency hints, merges results deterministically, and supports timeout/cancellation propagation to the model stream. 3) Result injection: tooling to synthesize a model message that injects tool outputs back into the chat/stream with metadata tags so evaluations and SDKs can surface results cleanly. 4) Retries and idempotency: retry helpers that consult tool-provided idempotency tokens and backoff prefs; non-idempotent tools will be retried only when explicitly allowed by the request hint. 5) Streaming stability: improved backpressure handling in the streaming path to avoid stalls when parallel tool calls finish at different times; this includes a buffered segment stream and small protocol change to emit partial tool markers so clients can reconcile partial outputs. 6) OpenAI compatibility layer: updated mapping so that consumers using the OpenAI-style 'function_call' API can opt into multi-tool semantics via the new 'tools' field while preserving legacy single-function behavior. 7) Docs and SDK: new API docs, TS/py SDK snippets, and a migration guide. Implementation notes: - Changes are backward compatible by default; legacy requests continue to work. - Internal feature flag "multi_tool_exec" gates the runtime path until we complete a canary rollout. - Added unit and integration tests covering scheduling, parallelism, and retry permutations. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan and telemetry collection.
commits: feat(tooling): add multi-tool execution executor and scheduler
chore(compat): extend openai-compat function_call envelope with tools array
feat(streaming): buffered segment stream and partial tool markers
docs(api): tool-calling multi-tool guide and migration notes
test: add integration tests for parallel tool groups and retries
fix(runtime): ensure cancellation propagates to in-flight tool tasks
review_comments: Diego Ramos: This is promising; can you clarify how dependency ordering is expressed when tools depend on other tool outputs?
Asha Patel: We support an optional 'depends_on' list per tool that names prior tool ids. Scheduler enforces ordering when dependencies are present.
Mei Chen: The partial tool markers look good but we need a clear contract for clients about finalization events to avoid double-processing.
Asha Patel: Added 'tool:finalized' event in the stream and documented the semantics in api/tool-calling.md.
Ravi Narayan: What about non-idempotent tool retries causing side effects? We should default to no automatic retries unless idempotency token present.
Asha Patel: Agreed. Default retry policy is 'none' for non-idempotent tools; callers can opt into 'safe-retry' with acknowledgement. Added tests for that behavior.
Mei Chen: CI flake on the new integration test — looks like a race in the test harness when two parallel groups finish simultaneously.
Asha Patel: Tightened the harness synchronization and added a deterministic seed; reran CI and tests passed.
Diego Ramos: Approved pending a tiny nit in the TS SDK typings to make 'parallel_groups' optional and more ergonomic.
Asha Patel: Fixed typings and added an example in the SDK README.
release_notes: Added multi-tool execution primitives: 'tools' array and 'parallel_groups' to enable parallel and dependent tool calls. Runtime scheduling, buffered streaming for partial tool outputs, and safe retry semantics added. Backwards compatible by default. See docs/multi-tool-migration.md for details.
